[
  {
    "hypothesis": "Predicted that an implemental mind-set would increase attitude strength (specifically decreasing ambivalence and increasing certainty) toward objects unrelated to the decision, and that this effect is driven by a one-sided evaluative focus.",
    "design": "between, three conditions: implemental mind-set with one-sided focus, implemental mind-set with two-sided focus, and neutral mind-set",
    "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were asked to choose a personal project and plan its implementation. In the one-sided focus condition, they listed three reasons why it was desirable and easy to implement. In the two-sided focus condition, they listed three reasons why it was desirable/easy and three reasons why it was undesirable/difficult. The neutral condition involved describing daily activities.",
    "outcome_measure": "Subjective ambivalence (measured via three 7-point scales) and attitude certainty (measured via one 7-point scale) regarding the issue of making a list of convicted sex offenders available to the general public.",
    "population_and_setting": "46 former and current students recruited via University of Chicago electronic postings.",
    "sample_size_total": 46,
    "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via University of Chicago electronic postings (newsgroup site, Facebook, and listserve notification); participated for $10.",
    "analysis_plan": "One-way ANOVA with mind-set condition as a between-participant variable, followed by specific comparisons between conditions.",
    "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
    "other_methods_notes": "Participants were instructed to respond to the study when no other people were around to minimize distractions. One participant was excluded for having direct contact with a sex offender."
  }
]
